title: Different Requirements for Taxi and Private Hire Drivers
what_it_is: Different Requirements for Taxi and Private Hire Drivers

sections.label: Motor vehicle third-party insurance
sections.summary: The Motor Vehicles Act requires all motor vehicles, including taxis and private hire cars, to be insured against third-party liability risks such as passenger death or bodily injury.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act requires all motor vehicles, including taxis and private hire cars, to be insured against third-party liability risks, which include death or bodily injury to passengers.

sections.label: Private hire car inspection requirements
sections.summary: Private hire cars have the same inspection requirements as private motorcars, while taxis must go for more frequent inspections.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The inspection requirements for private hire cars are the same as those for private motorcars, while taxis have to go for more frequent inspections.

sections.label: Shortened taxi and chauffeured courses
sections.summary: After the upcoming revamp, the taxi driving course will be shortened to about 25 hours and the chauffeured services course to about 10 hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: After the upcoming revamp, the taxi driving course will be shortened to about 25 hours, whereas the chauffeured services course will be about 10 hours long.

sections.label: No minimum age for drivers
sections.summary: As announced during MOT's Committee of Supply debate, there will be no minimum age requirement for private hire car drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: As announced during the Ministry of Transport (MOT)'s Committee of Supply debate recently, there will be no minimum age requirement for private hire car drivers.

sections.label: Taxi trips by street hail
sections.summary: Today, 80% of taxi trips are by street hail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Today, 80% of taxi trips are by street hail.

sections.label: Driving experience age limit
sections.summary: On the age limit, safety is better ensured by estimating how good a person is as a driver, so at least two years of driving experience is adequate and the situation will be monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: On the age limit, we think that safety is better ensured based on an estimate of how good a person is as a driver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: So, we think that the requirement for at least two years of driving experience is adequate and we will continue to monitor the situation.

sections.label: Two categories design choice
sections.summary: The system's initial design considered this, and two categories are thought to better serve the three articulated principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This was considered in our initial design of the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: It is possible, but at the moment, we think that two categories would be in better service of the three principles I have articulated.

sections.label: PRs and Work Permit drivers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether PRs and Work Permit holders with a PDVL may drive Uber or GrabCar, noting they cannot offer services as sole proprietors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is the Senior Minister of State saying that PRs and Work Permit holders who have the Private Hire Car Driver's Vocational Licence (PDVL) are allowed to drive an Uber or GrabCar?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: They are not allowed to offer their services via Uber and GrabCar as sole proprietors.
